page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6448H processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and hyperthreading is disabled, resulting in exactly one thread per core. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core. For hardware acceleration, it integrates a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, offering 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier performance in specific workloads, particularly LLM inference. For a small 135M model, the instance achieves prompt processing speeds of 13631.52 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 610.8 tokens per second. With a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 6293.73 tokens per second and text generation at 153.1 tokens per second, both placing in the top tier of tested servers. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also ranks in the top tier at 15.59 GB/sec. General CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU, fall within the average range.

The server offers high resource density by combining a high-capacity 48 GB VRAM GPU with 180.0 GB of system memory and local NVMe storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require substantial memory alongside GPU acceleration. However, a key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the relatively low 2.0 GHz base clock speed, which limits raw single-core CPU performance compared to dedicated compute-optimized instances. This hardware profile is best suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated database operations.
